simple.meaning: סֵפֶק (çêpheq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “chastisement ; also satiety.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Job, beginning at Job 20:22. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סֵפֶק (H5607) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סֵפֶק (çêpheq) / H5607 is traced through Job 20:22, Job 36:18 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5607. sepheq [ שֶׂ֫פֶק ] noun [masculine] doubtful word; hand-clapping , i.e. mockery (?) (compare verb Job 27:23 ); — שָׂ֑פֶק 36:18 in difficult clause בְשׂ מֶּןיְֿסִיתְךָ ׳כִּיחֵֿמָה because there is passion , (beware) lest it incite thee to mockery , Bae Kau Da (but בְּ הסית = incite against , hence Bu reads לִשְׂמֹּק ); De is not clear; others (as Di): lest it (passion) excite thee at the chastisement (see √ 2 ; compare Thes); Du reads לְחֵמָה מִשְׂמָּק lest chastisement incite thee to wrath . — On Job 20:22 (editions) see שֵׂפֶק . [ שֵׂ֫פֶק ] noun [masculine] sufficiency, plenty ; — suffix שִׂפְקוֺ Job 20:22 (Baer Gi; ׳ס van d. H.; opposed to צרר ). שַׂק see שׂקק . below
